research_rationale:
The frozen shared brief supplies conditional source propositions only. NIRA section 3 code authority, Schechter (May 27, 1935), and S.J.Res.113 (June 14, 1935) are not assigned automatically as first endpoints; the latter repeals code approval/enforcement and separately extends remaining Title I. EO7076 and EO7252 defeat categorical extinction of all administration. The unnamed-instruments and strike/insert rulings remain applicable. Original replacement and quotation recheck remain required. The complete order adopts the rendered report/recommendations/findings and "do[es] hereby cancel my order approving said Code." Both are present dispositive acts, with no future condition or delayed effectiveness. The printed date and matched APP metadata establish December 19, 1934. The hearings and report are affirmatively recited as past, not prospective duties. The cancellation is not held open for the subsequent code-regime repeal or for performance under other codes. The cancellation identifies the December 30, 1933 approval by date, code and subject, corroborated by complete held EO6543J. Adoption concerns the cancellation report; no separate future directive appears in the operative text. The transportation/construction passages describe expected operation of already approved other codes; they do not issue new approvals or order a future transfer. The narrow claim is completion of the cancellation/adoption acts, not a lifecycle finding for those other codes.

savings.reason: Cancellation continues to have the legal consequence that the December 30 approval is withdrawn. The recited Trucking and Construction Codes may govern operations under their own authority, and any accrued rights/liabilities under the former code are not adjudicated or extinguished here. These are residual consequences of the completed act, not outstanding directions of EO6925A. No general savings statute or universal liability preservation is asserted.
